title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 87-88
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 87 to 88 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 87 to 88 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 87 to 88.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 87 to 88** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः । अमृताशोऽमृतवपुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वतोमुखः ॥** **सुलभः सुव्रतः सिद्धः शत्रुजिच्छत्रुतापनः । न्यग्रोधोदुम्बरोऽश्वत्थश्चाणूरान्ध्रनिषूदनः ॥**

He blossoms like the lotus of the moon, the jasmine and its flower is he. The rain cloud, the purifier and the breeze is that God of gods. He takes the nectar, his form is nectar, all-knowing, with faces on every side. Easy to reach, of noble vows, perfect, the conqueror of foes is he. The one who scorches his enemies is that God of gods. He is the banyan, the fig and the peepal tree, and the slayer of Chanura.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 87 to 88 mean?
faq.a: He blossoms like the lotus of the moon, the jasmine and its flower is he. The rain cloud, the purifier and the breeze is that God of gods. He takes the nectar, his form is nectar, all-knowing, with faces on every side. Easy to reach, of noble vows, perfect, the conqueror of foes is he. The one who scorches his enemies is that God of gods. He is the banyan, the fig and the peepal tree, and the slayer of Chanura.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
